**Department Information**
--------------------------

  

  

**This position is open to current Colorado residents only** ***Most State of Colorado employees are eligible for a great benefit package! Please see the Supplemental Information section below for details!*** **Division of Child Welfare: Provider Services Unit**
The position is located in the Office of Children, Aging and Community Services(OCACS), Division of Child Welfare (DCW), Provider Services Unit (PSU), and Provider Performance Unit. The Division of Child Welfare Services provides a range of leadership, management, and supervisory functions related to the delivery of public child welfare services to children, youth, and families. The Division is responsible for the ongoing implementation of child welfare services in Colorado and supervises county departments of human/social services in the administration of Child Welfare programs, and privately operated agencies and facilities licensed and monitored by the Division of Child Welfare.  

  

The Provider Services Unit (PSU) exists to license, monitor, supervise, train, and provide statewide oversight for privately operated childcare facilities and agencies, including residential child care facilities (RCCF), qualified residential treatment programs (QRTP), secure residential treatment centers (SRTC), psychiatric residential treatment facilities (PRTF), homeless youth shelters (HYS), shelter care, specialized group facilities (group homes and group centers) (SGF), child placement agencies (CPA), foster homes (FH), therapeutic foster care (CPA\-THRFC), treatment foster care (TX\-FH), adoption agencies (CPAAD), respite child care centers (RCCC), day treatment facilities (DT), and Applied Behavior Analysis Clinics (ABA) across the State of Colorado. The goals of the unit are to ensure the health, safety, and well\-being of the children and youth served in those facilities. The work unit is responsible for comprehensive integrated (interagency) licensing and monitoring of the 24\-hour childcare facilities, auditing and investigating reports/allegations involving licensing violations, determining facility or agency culpability, evaluating the integration of trauma\-informed principles and practices, monitoring the quality of care, providing support and education, and ensuring the safety of children placed or receiving services with providers.

The ABA Investigative Monitoring Specialists that this supervisor oversees all maintain caseloads that include ABA Clinics.

jobs.description:
**Department Information**
--------------------------

  

This posting may be used to fill future vacancies at this location.  

This posting is only open to residents of the State of Colorado at the time of submitting your application.
If your goal is to build a career that makes a difference and builds greater public confidence in good government, consider joining the dedicated people of the State of Colorado. Our professionals strive to support state government and the citizens of Colorado. Customer service is a key component for every position in state government as is the focus on ideas and ways to redesign the delivery of services in making state government more effective and efficient.
In addition to a great agency and rewarding, meaningful work, we offer:* Distinctive career advancement opportunities throughout the state system;
* Strong, secure, yet flexible retirement benefits including PERA Defined Benefit Plan or PERA Defined;
* Contribution Plan plus 401K and 457 plans. Member Contribution Rates. Correctional Officers I\-IV qualify as "Safety Officers" and are eligible for increased PERA benefits;
* Medical and dental health plans;
* Short and long term disability coverage;
* Paid life insurance;
* 11 paid holidays per year plus vacation and sick leave;
* Wellness program, tuition reimbursement, training opportunities and more;
* Visit State of Colorado Employee Benefits. for more information;
* This position is compensated on a bi\-weekly pay cycle.

**Description of Job**
----------------------


The Parole Case Manager provides structured community\-based case management and supervision to individuals released to parole who have been assessed as requiring low\-level supervision based on the current Community Supervision Tool, demonstrated stability in the community, compliance with supervision requirements, and progress toward successful completion of parole.


The position promotes successful community reintegration and public safety through evidence\-based case management, individualized case planning, regular client contact, monitoring of conditions and Parole Board requirements, identification of changing risk and needs, connection to community resources, and timely intervention when concerns arise.


Parole Case Managers work collaboratively with Community Parole Officers, supervisors, treatment providers, community partners, and other criminal justice professionals and supports the Division's graduated supervision model by matching supervision resources to assessed risk and need, promoting successful completion of parole.

**Job duties and responsibilities include but are not limited to:*** Managing an assigned caseload of individuals released to parole in accordance with statute, administrative regulation, Division policy, supervision standards, and evidence\-based correctional practices.
* Conducting scheduled contacts with individuals under supervision and maintains required case contact standards based upon assigned supervision level and individual case circumstances.
* Develop, review, and update individualized case plans designed to address assessed criminogenic needs, reinforce protective factors, promote stability, and support successful completion of parole.
* Use motivational interviewing, effective communication, problem\-solving, and other evidence\-based practices to encourage behavioral change and increase individual accountability.
* Monitor compliance with conditions of parole, Parole Board directives, treatment requirements, employment or educational expectations, residence requirements, financial obligations, and other individualized supervision requirements.
* Review available information to identify changes in behavior, circumstances, risk factors, or needs that may require intervention or a change in the supervision strategy.
* Assist individuals in identifying and accessing appropriate community resources, including behavioral health treatment, substance use treatment, employment, education, housing, transportation, identification documents, benefits, and other stabilizing services.
* Consult with supervisory staff and Community Parole Officers regarding cases requiring enhanced supervision or enforcement\-related action.
* Maintain accurate, complete, and timely case records.
* Participate in case conferences, multidisciplinary meetings, training, quality\-assurance activities, and other Division initiatives.
* Performs other duties as assigned.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

A1A1XX Corrections Case Manager I **Minimum Qualifications:**

**Experience Only:**  

  

Three (3\) years of relevant professional experience conducting inmate intake, applying risk/ need assessments (such as LSI, ORAS\-CST, CTAP), drafting individualized case plans utilized evidence\-based practices in a direct client\-facing environment such criminal justice, corrections, probation/parole, case management, social services, behavioral health, community supervision, reentry services or closely related work

A combination of education in criminal justice, criminology, sociology, psychology, social work, human services, behavioral sciences, or another closely related field and experience as defined above equal to three (3\) years  

  

**Required Competencies*** Ability to manage an assigned caseload, prioritize responsibilities, maintain accurate records, and meet established deadlines and contact standards.

Responsibilities:

The Social Worker, MSW plans, organizes and implements social work services to participants and their caregivers in accordance with InnovAge policies and all applicable regulations. Conducts psychosocial assessments, participates in care planning and acts as a liaison between the participant and the interdisciplinary team.  

This role requires being on\-site at the center and field\-based work, including visits to participants’ homes and other locations, to ensure continuity of care and support. **Essential Functions and Work Responsibilities****Functional Category: Assessment \& Care Planning*** Conducts initial psychosocial assessments (including SLUMS, PHQ\-9, housing, food, financial security, MDPOA/decision\-maker status).
* Completes in\-person reassessments at least every six months or as required.
* Performs in\-home visits as required by regulations or as indicated
* Participates in IDT meetings, morning huddles, mini\-teams, and PDPM meetings to ensure coordinated care.
* Facilitates and documents participant care conferences, family meetings, and facility partnership meetings.
* Participates in discharge planning and plan of care development, ensuring problems, interventions, and goals are well defined.
* Supports participants transitioning between residences or care facilities, including arranging transportation and coordinating moves when no support system is available.


Functional Category: Case Management \& Care Coordination* Serves as primary liaison between participant/family and the IDT, facilitating communication and resolution of care issues.
* Coordinates respite SNF, ALF admissions, including transportation and discharge planning.
* Documents housing encounters in EPIC
* Collaborate with comfort care team for end\-of\-life activities
* Assists participant’s family with end\-of\-life coordination
* Collaborates with RN Case Management on hospitalizations, and provides psychosocial input
* May serve as back\-up to RNCM.
* Reviews participant/family concerns with Ombudsman and escalates facility quality concerns; maintains admission holds on facilities with care issues and manages urgent rehousing when contracts terminate.
* Coordinates guardianship process for participants lacking decision\-making capacity without a surrogate.
* Obtains SNF/ALF updates for IDT, manages respite scheduling, and ensures placement transitions are supported.
* Provides options counseling when appropriate
* Assists participants who are disenrolling with timely referrals to external services and completion of disenrollment paperwork.

* Assists participants and caregivers with grievances and appeals, explaining rights and processes.
* Provides notification and explanation of participant rights regarding Level of Care (LOC) denials or disenrollment declines.


Functional Category: Documentation \& Compliance* Maintains accurate and timely documentation in Epic, EireneRx, and other systems (demographic updates, address/phone changes, participant chart updates).
* Complete PASSR screenings, supportive housing forms and other like documents as mandated by federal and state agencies within regulatory timelines.

jobs.title: Team Leader / Senior Evaluation Specialist
jobs.description:
Integrated Business \& Technical Consultants, Inc. (IBTCI), a U.S.\-based international development consulting company established in 1987, has worked in over 100 countries and implemented over 300 projects. IBTCI serves government agencies, private\-sector companies, and donor organizations. IBTCI specializes in monitoring, evaluation, research, and learning (MERL) and institutional support across sectors including conflict and crisis, democracy and governance, agriculture, economic growth, food security, education, environment, and global health.


**Assignment Title: Team Leader / Senior Evaluation Specialist**


**Department/Location: Remote, with potential travel to Ethiopia, Ukraine, Haiti, the Philippines, and/or Türkiye**


**Technical Point of Contact: Project Director**


**Type: Consultant, Short\-term / Intermittent**

**Classification: Consultancy**


**Overview:** IBTCI is seeking a Team Leader / Senior Evaluation Specialist for a proposed assignment to develop and test a standardized livelihoods MEAL framework and evaluate 13 humanitarian livelihoods projects in Ethiopia, Ukraine, Haiti, the Philippines, and Türkiye. The Team Leader will provide overall technical and managerial leadership for the portfolio\-level Theory of Change, project logic\-model framework, evaluation toolsets, and concurrent mixed\-methods evaluations. The ideal candidate combines senior MERL and evaluation leadership with livelihoods subject\-matter knowledge, project\-design expertise, and experience working in one or more target countries or comparable humanitarian and fragile contexts. This is an intermittent, part\-time consultancy anticipated to begin in October 2026 and continue through completion of assigned deliverables, subject to project implementation schedules.


**Essential Duties/Tasks and Responsibilities:**


* Provide overall technical direction, quality assurance, work planning, and team coordination across framework development and all assigned project evaluations.
* Lead stakeholder consultations and the development and validation of a single portfolio\-level livelihoods Theory of Change and a project\-level logic\-model framework linking inputs, activities, outputs, short\-term outcomes, and long\-term outcomes.
* Direct development and field testing of the pre\-project vetting toolset, monitoring checklist, short\- and long\-term outcome toolsets, cost\-effectiveness toolset, user guides, and common indicator menu, ensuring practical use by professional evaluators and non\-evaluator personnel.
* Ensure the framework and tools support cross\-country comparability, culturally appropriate application, high inter\-rater reliability, and ethical identification of comparison populations where feasible.
* Lead or approve cluster and project evaluation plans, including evaluation questions, mixed\-methods designs, sampling, data sources, instrument packages, analysis plans, limitations, and appropriate tiers of rigor based on project size, data availability, security, and feasibility.
* Oversee independent primary data collection where required; validation of implementing\-organization data; and proportionate review of project financial documentation.
* Ensure compliance with applicable IRB or ethics approvals, informed\-consent procedures, confidentiality, data protection, safeguarding, duty\-of\-care, and implementing\-organization policies.
* Direct framework revisions based on pilot evaluations and ensure complete, coherent, evidence\-traceable deliverables, including monthly progress updates, scorecards, project evaluation reports, learning and executive\-summary slide decks, and cluster and portfolio presentations.
* Facilitate learning discussions and presentations; translate evidence into practical recommendations for project design, portfolio management, partner selection, and future use of the livelihoods framework.


**Minimum Qualifications:**


* At least **15 years** of progressively responsible experience in MERL, evaluation, applied research, or program design, including leadership of complex, multi\-country or multi\-project evaluations.
* Demonstrated experience developing or validating Theories of Change, logic models, results frameworks, evaluation frameworks, and project designs.
* Demonstrated expertise in at least one methodological domain \- qualitative or quantitative \- and sufficient mixed\-methods experience to lead integration, triangulation, and interpretation across both domains.
* Substantial subject\-matter experience in livelihoods, economic strengthening, agriculture, food security, resilience, market systems, enterprise development, or closely related programming.
* Experience designing and leading process, performance, outcome, and/or impact\-oriented evaluations, including context\-appropriate approaches to causal inference and contribution.
* Experience working with international NGOs, multilateral organizations, local governments, and community\-based organizations.
* Demonstrated ability to manage multidisciplinary senior experts, analysts, country coordinators, and field data\-collection teams working concurrently.
* Professional experience in at least one target country or region, or in comparable fragile, conflict\-affected, humanitarian, and/or culturally diverse contexts.
* Excellent analytical, facilitation, presentation, and written and oral communication skills in English.


**Education:** Master's degree or higher in evaluation, economics, international development, public policy, social sciences, agriculture, livelihoods, statistics, or another relevant field.


**Preferred Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:**


* PhD in development research, experimental or quasi\-experimental design, evaluation, livelihoods, or a related subject\-matter field.
* Experience developing standardized global evaluation frameworks, scorecards, indicator menus, and tools intended for repeated use across countries and implementers.
* Familiarity with OECD DAC

**Department Information**
--------------------------

  

This posting may be used to fill future vacancies at this location.  

This posting is only open to residents of the State of Colorado at the time of submitting your application.
If your goal is to build a career that makes a difference and builds greater public confidence in good government, consider joining the dedicated people of the State of Colorado. Our professionals strive to support state government and the citizens of Colorado. Customer service is a key component for every position in state government as is the focus on ideas and ways to redesign the delivery of services in making state government more effective and efficient.
In addition to a great agency and rewarding, meaningful work, we offer:* Distinctive career advancement opportunities throughout the state system;
* Strong, secure, yet flexible retirement benefits including PERA Defined Benefit Plan or PERA Defined;
* Contribution Plan plus 401K and 457 plans. Member Contribution Rates. Correctional Officers I\-IV qualify as "Safety Officers" and are eligible for increased PERA benefits;
* Medical and dental health plans;
* Short and long term disability coverage;
* Paid life insurance;
* 11 paid holidays per year plus vacation and sick leave;
* Wellness program, tuition reimbursement, training opportunities and more;
* Visit State of Colorado Employee Benefits. for more information;
* This position is compensated on a bi\-weekly pay cycle.

**Description of Job**
----------------------


The Parole Case Manager provides structured community\-based case management and supervision to individuals released to parole who have been assessed as requiring low\-level supervision based on the current Community Supervision Tool, demonstrated stability in the community, compliance with supervision requirements, and progress toward successful completion of parole.


The position promotes successful community reintegration and public safety through evidence\-based case management, individualized case planning, regular client contact, monitoring of conditions and Parole Board requirements, identification of changing risk and needs, connection to community resources, and timely intervention when concerns arise.


Parole Case Managers work collaboratively with Community Parole Officers, supervisors, treatment providers, community partners, and other criminal justice professionals and supports the Division's graduated supervision model by matching supervision resources to assessed risk and need, promoting successful completion of parole.

**Job duties and responsibilities include but are not limited to:*** Managing an assigned caseload of individuals released to parole in accordance with statute, administrative regulation, Division policy, supervision standards, and evidence\-based correctional practices.
* Conducting scheduled contacts with individuals under supervision and maintains required case contact standards based upon assigned supervision level and individual case circumstances.
* Develop, review, and update individualized case plans designed to address assessed criminogenic needs, reinforce protective factors, promote stability, and support successful completion of parole.
* Use motivational interviewing, effective communication, problem\-solving, and other evidence\-based practices to encourage behavioral change and increase individual accountability.
* Monitor compliance with conditions of parole, Parole Board directives, treatment requirements, employment or educational expectations, residence requirements, financial obligations, and other individualized supervision requirements.
* Review available information to identify changes in behavior, circumstances, risk factors, or needs that may require intervention or a change in the supervision strategy.
* Assist individuals in identifying and accessing appropriate community resources, including behavioral health treatment, substance use treatment, employment, education, housing, transportation, identification documents, benefits, and other stabilizing services.
* Consult with supervisory staff and Community Parole Officers regarding cases requiring enhanced supervision or enforcement\-related action.
* Maintain accurate, complete, and timely case records.
* Participate in case conferences, multidisciplinary meetings, training, quality\-assurance activities, and other Division initiatives.
* Performs other duties as assigned.

**Minimum Qualifications, Substitutions, Conditions of Employment \& Appeal Rights**
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------


**Residency Requirement:**
This posting is only open to residents of the State of Colorado at the time of submitting your application. **Class Code \& Classification Description:**  

A1A1XX Corrections Case Manager I **Minimum Qualifications:**

**Experience Only:**  

  

Three (3\) years of relevant professional experience conducting inmate intake, applying risk/ need assessments (such as LSI, ORAS\-CST, CTAP), drafting individualized case plans utilized evidence\-based practices in a direct client\-facing environment such criminal justice, corrections, probation/parole, case management, social services, behavioral health, community supervision, reentry services or closely related work  

  

**Or**  

  

**Education and Experience:**  

  

A combination of education in criminal justice, criminology, sociology, psychology, social work, human services, behavioral sciences, or another closely related field and experience as defined above equal to three (3\) years  

  

**Required Competencies*** Ability to manage an assigned caseload, prioritize responsibilities, maintain accurate records, and meet established deadlines and contact standards.
* Ability to interpret assessment information, recognize changes in risk or circumstances, identify concerns, and determine when supervisory consultation or transfer to a higher level of s

Responsibilities:

The Social Worker, MSW plans, organizes and implements social work services to participants and their caregivers in accordance with InnovAge policies and all applicable regulations. Conducts psychosocial assessments, participates in care planning and acts as a liaison between the participant and the interdisciplinary team.  

This role requires being on\-site at the center and field\-based work, including visits to participants’ homes and other locations, to ensure continuity of care and support. **Essential Functions and Work Responsibilities****Functional Category: Assessment \& Care Planning*** Conducts initial psychosocial assessments (including SLUMS, PHQ\-9, housing, food, financial security, MDPOA/decision\-maker status).
* Completes in\-person reassessments at least every six months or as required.
* Performs in\-home visits as required by regulations or as indicated
* Participates in IDT meetings, morning huddles, mini\-teams, and PDPM meetings to ensure coordinated care.
* Facilitates and documents participant care conferences, family meetings, and facility partnership meetings.
* Participates in discharge planning and plan of care development, ensuring problems, interventions, and goals are well defined.
* Supports participants transitioning between residences or care facilities, including arranging transportation and coordinating moves when no support system is available.


Functional Category: Case Management \& Care Coordination* Serves as primary liaison between participant/family and the IDT, facilitating communication and resolution of care issues.
* Coordinates respite SNF, ALF admissions, including transportation and discharge planning.
* Documents housing encounters in EPIC
* Collaborate with comfort care team for end\-of\-life activities
* Assists participant’s family with end\-of\-life coordination
* Collaborates with RN Case Management on hospitalizations, and provides psychosocial input
* May serve as back\-up to RNCM.
* Reviews participant/family concerns with Ombudsman and escalates facility quality concerns; maintains admission holds on facilities with care issues and manages urgent rehousing when contracts terminate.
* Coordinates guardianship process for participants lacking decision\-making capacity without a surrogate.
* Obtains SNF/ALF updates for IDT, manages respite scheduling, and ensures placement transitions are supported.
* Provides options counseling when appropriate
* Assists participants who are disenrolling with timely referrals to external services and completion of disenrollment paperwork.


Functional Category: Psychosocial Support \& Advocacy* Provides counseling and psychosocial support in coordination with behavioral health for participants and caregivers as indicated
* Completes comfort care assessments and provides guidance on transitions to end\-of\-life services.
* Advocates for participants living in unsafe housing conditions
* Contributed to RCAs development, incident reporting, and follow\-up for abuse, neglect, exploitation, and elopements.
* Assists participants and caregivers with grievances and appeals, explaining rights and processes.
* Provides notification and explanation of participant rights regarding Level of Care (LOC) denials or disenrollment declines.


Functional Category: Documentation \& Compliance* Maintains accurate and timely documentation in Epic, EireneRx, and other systems (demographic updates, address/phone changes, participant chart updates).
* Complete PASSR screenings, supportive housing forms and other like documents as mandated by federal and state agencies within regulatory timelines.
* Supports Medicaid eligibility recertification processes,
* Partners with Eligibility Financial Determination teams to educate participants/families on required information/documentation needed to maintain and restore Medicaid eligibility
* dictation, and assists with resource compliance.
* Accurate and timely reporting of disenrollments in required systems
* Escalates to Center Director service recovery is needed for a participant concern or disenrollment
* Ensures all participant care coordination complies with CMS, HCPF, and InnovAge policy requirements.


Functional Category: Professional Development \& Team Collaboration* Participates in IDT and department meetings, cross\-site collaboratives, trainings, and annual competencies.
* Provides community education and participates in external support groups, inter\-agency coordination, and partnership meetings with RCFEs as indicated
* Coordinates with facilities on participant needs.
* Provides caseload coverage support as assigned for MSW PTO, open FTEs, and general team needs.


Performs other duties as assigned **Travel Requirements****Travel*** Travel may be required
* Overnight travel may include local or out of state

new_jobs.description:
We are recruiting for a mission\-driven Supervisor, Addiction \- Denver CARES to join our team!  

  

We're with you for life’s journey. At Denver Health, purpose isn’t just something we believe in—it’s something we live every day, for life’s journey.


**Our Values**

Respect \| Belonging \| Accountability \| Transparency


**Department**

Denver CARES TRT Providers
**Job Summary**  

  

Under general supervision, provides administrative, clinical, and supportive supervision to addictions program clinical staff at the Denver CARES or OBHS clinic(s). Establishes a coaching/mentoring/learning alliance with staff to increase knowledge, skills, abilities, and attitudes. Motivates employees through open communication, timely feedback, and leading by example. Participates in policy planning and implementation. Plans, schedules, coordinates, and assigns work to assure service provision, including coverage. Strives to create a positive customer experience by committing to higher standards and communicating compelling vision.
  

  

**Essential Functions** :
  

* Provides administrative, clinical, and supportive supervision to addictions program clinical staff. (10%)
* Assists in developing, implementing and interpreting policies, procedures, and programs to assure program compliance with all Denver Health policies and the state of Colorado substance abuse treatment rules and regulations. (10%)
* Engages in leadership standard work as adopted by the organization (patient and staff rounding, visual management board, daily huddles). (10%)
* Routinely communicates with the management/leadership team regarding staff service activities, and problems needing department leadership attention. (10%)
* Delegates authority and responsibility as appropriate. (10%)
* Builds productive cohesive teams. (10%)
* Routinely meets with staff for review of cases, problem solving, clinical supervision, job performance, ongoing communication and consultation. (5%)
* Identifies areas for team and/or individual growth and development. (5%)
* Promptly addresses staff performance, attendance, or behavioral issues. (5%)
* Provides timely and appropriate feedback with courtesy and respect. (5%)
* Completes employee performance reviews, annually and as needed. (5%)
* Assures that new or reassigned employees receive appropriate orientation to job responsibilities. (5%)
* Plans, schedules, coordinates and assigns work to assure service provision, including coverage. (5%)
* Monitors caseloads and recommends adjustments as needed. (5%)

  

**Education** :
  

* Master's Degree Required

  

**Work Experience** :
  

* 1\-3 years Three years of post\-master’s direct social work or counseling experience in an organized clinical setting Required

  

**Licenses** :
  

* LCSW\-Licensed Clinical Social Worker \- LCSW State Licensing Board Required and
* LPC\-Licensed Professional Counselor \- LPC State Licensing Board Required and
* CACIII\-Certified Addiction Counselor III \- NAADAC \- The Association for Addiction Professionals Required

* Knowledge of supervision tactics and ongoing development of supervision abilities.
* Knowledge of clinical social work and/or clinical counseling and the patient population served.
* Knowledge of applicable substance abuse treatment rules and regulations pertaining to the programs(s) supervised.
* Knowledge of change in leadership and/or learn management.
* Excellent interpersonal and team building skills.
* Skill in identifying problems and opportunities to improve care.
* Ability to encourage and enhance work performance through feedback, mentoring, coaching, and through example.
* Proficient in Microsoft Excel, Word, PowerPoint, required.

Regular
